newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil loadings normal despite strike.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil loadings normal despite strike.

text.p: Venezuela's oil export ports were operating normally on Wednesday morning despite a national strike which has paralyzed much of the country, port officials said.
In Lake Maracaibo, the country's largest oil export route, a port official said oil tankers were entering and leaving the lake normally and ship pilots were still working.
"Everything is working normally here in terms of petroleum loadings and pilotage," an official at the port captain's office told Reuters.
A shipping agent in Maracaibo said: "It feels just like a holiday. Some people have taken advantage of a day off by going to the beach, but in the oil terminals, everything is working normally."
The strike was called by the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), the country's largest trades' union, in protest at the private sector's failure to raise salaries.

Fedepetrol, the main oil workers' union, said it planned to join the 12-hour stoppage and the state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) activated its contingency plan to ensure continued operations.
In previous strikes, PDVSA's has successfully avoided any disruption in its 3.2 million barrel per day operation by replacing striking workers with non-unionized senior employees.
